title: Access velocity and quality triage - POC weekly sync
topics: KV cache warmup and quantization profile
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on gating access velocity and addressing quality regressions seen in the last bench run. Customer progressing on staging creds but still blocked on KMS integration and RBAC. SE proposed mitigations (prefix caching warmup, temporary gateway token) and next steps include security pack, scoped benchmark window, and a staged end-to-end test next Tuesday.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share security pack (SOC2 report, infra diagram, dataflow map); due: 2026-03-16
Liam O'Neill: Run targeted 4-hour latency window for 1k requests with current quant profile and share raw logs; due: 2026-03-17
Tom Lin: Provision staging IAM role and SSO binding for redwood-staging@bluepeak; due: 2026-03-15
Olivia Park: Confirm KMS key policy and whether HSM is required; due: 2026-03-18
Sara Gutierrez: Run internal smoke tests after creds and report any 500s; due: 2026-03-18
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + minimal network diagram (Maya) by 3/16
SE to schedule bench run and upload raw traces to shared drive (Liam) by 3/17
Customer to grant staging role and KMS read policy by 3/15 (Tom/Olivia)
Schedule end-to-end demo with product and devops once staging tests pass (tentative 2026-03-23)
Follow-up sync in one week to review bench results and rollout plan
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill (Redwood); Sara Gutierrez, Dr. Amit Rao, Tom Lin, Olivia Park, Kayla Moreno (BluePeak)

Summary: quick triage on access velocity and some quality blips that showed up in the last batch. aim: unblock staging creds and agree on a narrow benchmark window.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick readout: we had a benchmark yesterday that showed higher tail latency for a subset of requests, wanted to go through the logs and lift any access blockers.
[01:12] Sara Gutierrez: Yeah, thanks Maya. we provisioned most of the staging infra but we're waiting on the KMS policy and the SSO binding, so we can't yet run full end-to-end flows.
[02:05] Liam O'Neill: Ok, that explains some 403s in the traces, mutations to the gateway token cause retries and that bumps observed p90. are you on a customer-managed KMS?
[02:38] Olivia Park: we're on an AWS KMS key in the same account. question — do you need symmetric decrypt permission or full admin?
[03:08] Liam O'Neill: decrypt + describe is enough for the integration, admin isn't necessary. HSM only if you have policies requiring it, we can support that but it'll add a config step.
[04:20] Dr. Amit Rao: quick question on quantization — we saw lower token quality when you switched to int8 for one of the models. any insight?
[04:48] Liam O'Neill: yeah, so quant profiles vary by model and prompt distribution. our recommendation was the mixed-quant profile for your prompt lengths — saves ~35% cost but it can shift logits for some rare tokens. we can narrow the profile or run delta-eval with your prompt set.
[06:01] Kayla Moreno: if quality drops slightly, product might push back. what's the rollback plan?
[06:20] Maya Chen: can always route to a higher-precision model for those flows or fallback to hosted variant. routing policy + canary is our standard.
[07:00] Tom Lin: circling back to access — I provisioned the staging VPC peering but still need to attach the role for redwood-staging service account. when you say SSO binding, is that SAML or OIDC?
[07:30] Sara Gutierrez: we use OIDC via our identity provider, so we'll need a client id and redirect set up.
[08:05] Liam O'Neill: OIDC is fine; we'll provide a minimal doc for the redirect/claim mapping. shouldn't take long once you share the client id.
[09:10] Dr. Amit Rao: the bench showed that KV cache warmup reduced p99 by ~200ms after about 120 requests. can we pre-warm before critical flows?
[09:45] Liam O'Neill: yep, prefix/KV warming is doable — you can seed the cache during deploy or via a short warmup job. also we noticed a few weird spikes from long context windows mixing with reranking.
[10:28] Sara Gutierrez: reranking is run on our side after generation, any suggestions to reduce the latency there?
[10:46] Liam O'Neill: you could move reranker to be an async stage or run in batch with smaller beam size. also consider sending compact embeddings instead of full context for faster rerank decisions.
[11:35] Kayla Moreno: also worth noting our compliance team needs the audit logs to show data access. does Redwood attach request-level metadata to logs?
[11:50] Maya Chen: yes, we can surface per-token cost and request id; we also support audit log export to your SIEM. we'll put that in the security pack.
[12:40] Tom Lin: about the 500s, some traces show a gateway timeout around 18s. what's the default timeout on your side?
[12:58] Liam O'Neill: default is 30s but the gateway can cut earlier if it sees backend stalls; those 18s look like retry cascades from permission errors.
[13:45] Sara Gutierrez: ok. we'll prioritize the KMS tiny policy updates and SSO client id by end of Monday.
[14:10] Dr. Amit Rao: quick thought — can you run a focused bench only on our 4 top prompt families? that'll give better signal than a wide sweep.
[14:35] Liam O'Neill: absolutely, if you share sample prompts and typical lengths we'll run an apples-to-apples. include expected distribution of tokens per request.
[15:05] Maya Chen: I'll collect the security docs and the sample prompts and send both; also we'll include a short deck on toggles (quant, cache, routing).
[16:20] Kayla Moreno: any blockers for rolling a temporary gateway token so you can run the bench while we finalize KMS?
[16:45] Maya Chen: yes we can do a scoped gateway token limited to staging IP ranges; it's a standard mitigant. we'll need an approved list of IP ranges and an expiration.
[18:00] Tom Lin: we can provide ranges today. about the bench window, are you flexible on duration? our infra wants a 4-hour window with steady traffic to measure drift.
[18:24] Liam O'Neill: 4 hours is fine — we'll schedule a controlled run and capture traces + raw token timings.
[19:40] Sara Gutierrez: also want to capture memory/transfer metrics from the client side; we'll add that to the runbook.
[20:05] Liam O'Neill: perfect. we'll also attach model versioning tags to each trace so you can correlate outputs to the exact variant.
[21:30] Dr. Amit Rao: on SLOs — our internal target is p95 under 400ms for interactive flows, p99 under 800ms. can Redwood expose per-route SLO dashboards?
[21:50] Maya Chen: yes, Console has per-route latency and token breakdowns. we'll grant you access to a demo dashboard.
[22:30] Kayla Moreno: will that show cost estimates per route too?
[22:45] Maya Chen: yep, token-level cost and estimated monthly spend are visible.
[23:10] Tom Lin: one oddity — in the last run there was a region fallback to us-west when we expected eu-west. any explanation?
[23:35] Liam O'Neill: routing policy fallback can trigger if eu-west pool was low; we can pin requests to the eu-west pool for the bench to avoid cross-region variance.
[24:10] Sara Gutierrez: please pin for the test. we want stable latencies.
[24:35] Liam O'Neill: noted. we'll configure pinning and disable fallback for the scheduled window.
[25:05] Maya Chen: recap of outstanding items: 1) staging role + oidc client id from BluePeak, 2) KMS policy decision, 3) sample prompts and token distributions, 4) IP ranges for scoped gateway token, 5) Redwood will send security pack + bench schedule.
[26:00] Olivia Park: small compliance Q — do you retain raw customer prompts in logs by default?
[26:18] Liam O'Neill: we redact user content by default in long-term storage but can enable shorter-term full traces under a retention agreement; we'll detail in the pack.
[27:05] Sara Gutierrez: good. any preference on the quant profile to start with?
[27:22] Liam O'Neill: start mixed-quant, but for critical flows route to high-precision variant or keep a per-route override. we'll show how to toggle in the Console.
[28:40] Tom Lin: timeline ask — if we get creds by Monday can we run the bench Wednesday?
[29:00] Maya Chen: yes that works. we'll aim for Wednesday morning UTC for the 4h window.
[30:12] Kayla Moreno: for the E2E demo afterwards can product drive acceptance criteria? I'd like a checklist: correctness on top-3 prompts, no p99 spikes > 1s, and RBAC logs present.
[30:40] Maya Chen: agreed — we'll use that as the acceptance checklist for the demo.
[31:15] Dr. Amit Rao: small nit — some tokenization differences affected rerank scores, could you normalize tokenizer versions across models?
[31:36] Liam O'Neill: yes we can enforce the same tokenizer and we'll include tokenization configs in the trace metadata.
[32:20] Sara Gutierrez: anything else on the network side? we may need a temporary NAT egress rule for the bench.
[32:50] Tom Lin: we'll add the NAT rule and share the ranges.
[33:30] Maya Chen: thanks Tom. quick note: we'll also surface a failover playbook if the bench shows throughput issues — options include increasing pool size or routing more flows to dedicated variant.
[34:15] Kayla Moreno: ok. security will validate the limited gateway token approach.
[34:40] Olivia Park: if we do a temporary token, I want expiration and immediate revocation path documented.
[35:05] Maya Chen: yes we'll include revocation steps and who to contact.
[36:12] Liam O'Neill: one more technical note — when we collect traces, we'll attach raw kv-cache hit rates so you can see warmup effect.
[36:45] Sara Gutierrez: that's helpful.
[37:20] Dr. Amit Rao: can Redwood also run a small A/B to validate quality differences between mixed-quant and high-precision on our top prompts?
[37:40] Liam O'Neill: yes, we can run a split test across 10k examples and provide delta metrics (perplexity surrogate + human spot checks) — that'll take about 48 hours of processing.
[38:55] Kayla Moreno: human spot checks — who owns that? product or us?
[39:10] Maya Chen: we can coordinate a shared rubric; product can do spot checks and Redwood provides numeric deltas.
[40:00] Sara Gutierrez: ok. lastly, can you add an item in the PRD to note fallback routing behavior? we had unexpected cross-region fallback earlier.
[40:20] Maya Chen: will do.
[41:00] Tom Lin: anything else?
[41:10] Olivia Park: not from security, just to see the pack.
[41:30] Dr. Amit Rao: all good.
[42:00] Maya Chen: great — to summarize: Maya sends security pack + toggles deck by 3/16; Tom + Olivia to grant staging creds and KMS policy by 3/15; Sara to run smoke after creds; Liam runs the 4-hour bench on Wed (3/18) and uploads traces; follow-up sync same time next week.
[43:15] Kayla Moreno: confirmed.
[44:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll share notes and action items. ending call.
[44:30] (call ends)
